title: WHO Guideline on Use of Ferritin Concentrations and Hemoglobin Cutoffs to Assess Iron Status
section_heading: WHO Diagnostic Thresholds - Hemoglobin Cutoffs by Age and Physiological State
content: The World Health Organization defines anemia based on epidemiological venous blood hemoglobin concentrations: Children 6-59 months of age: Hb < 11.0 g/dL; Children 5-11 years of age: Hb < 11.5 g/dL; Children 12-14 years of age and non-pregnant adult women: Hb < 12.0 g/dL; Pregnant women: Hb < 11.0 g/dL (Hb < 10.5 g/dL in second trimester); Adult men: Hb < 13.0 g/dL. Severity of anemia in non-pregnant adult females is categorized as mild (Hb 11.0-11.9 g/dL), moderate (Hb 8.0-10.9 g/dL), and severe (Hb < 8.0 g/dL). Serum ferritin below 15 ug/L in adults indicates depleted iron stores.
